course_name_original: Expresión gráfica y diseño asistido por ordenador
prerequisites: General prior knowledge of high school Technical Drawing contents is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for spatial vision and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications.
Master the resolution of graphic problems that may arise in engineering.
Develop skills and abilities that allow expressing graphic solutions with precision, clarity, and objectivity.
Acquire the ability to abstract in order to visualize objects from different positions in space.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Innovation and Creativity. Design and carry out a new task or project differently using creativity and curiosity to add value with an entrepreneurial attitude.

teaching_methods: Exams, deliverables, tutorials, and personal work
assessment_rules: For Graphic Expression deliverables and the Global Exam, a minimum of 4.0 must be obtained in each exercise/block, and an average of 5.0. A Partial Exam may free up blocks for the Global Exam if a minimum of 4.0 is achieved. For Computer-Aided Design, the preferential system is the weighted average of practice session submissions, requiring a minimum score of 5.0; otherwise, a specific practical CAD exercise must be submitted. In the event of not passing the Global Exam in the ordinary call, blocks with at least 4.0 do not need to be retaken in the extraordinary call. Students must demonstrate authorship of their work in an oral interview, failing which the work will receive a 0.
